original_source_text: Recent advances in GPU-accelerated hypergraph partitioning have achieved substantial performance gains but remain limited to full partitioning. In particular, the lack of support for incrementality is a critical limitation for being used by many CAD applications, where circuit hypergraphs iteratively undergo incremental modifications as part of optimization loops. To overcome this limitation, we present iHyperG, the first GPU-parallel incremental k-way hypergraph partitioner. iHyperG introduces a scalable delta-based hypergraph data structure for efficient incremental modifications on a GPU, along with an effective incremental partitioning algorithm that rebalances partitions in a single pass and refines only cut-critical vertices. Experimental results show that iHyperG achieves average speedups of 190x for modification and 83x for partitioning over a state-of-the-art GPU-parallel hypergraph partitioner, while maintaining comparable partitioning quality.
